articles.title: An updated Model Spec for more capable and beneficial AI
articles.summary: OpenAI’s updated Model Spec outlines five core values to guide more capable AI toward sound judgment, human agency, and faithfulness to human intent.
articles.content:
Title: An updated Model Spec for more capable and beneficial AI

URL Source: https://openai.com/index/updated-model-spec

Markdown Content:
As our models get smarter and take more consequential actions in the world, it becomes increasingly important that they go beyond just interpreting the specific instructions they receive. Models also need to understand human intentions and values, so they can exercise good judgment in situations their instructions don’t explicitly address while remaining faithful to human intent and oversight.

Today we’re updating the [Model Spec⁠(opens in a new window)](https://model-spec.openai.com/2026-10-29.html), our public description of how we want our models to behave. The update reorganizes its guidance around five underlying values: **faithfulness to human intent**, **harm minimization**, **honesty and transparency**, **human agency**, and **care**. This reflects an aim of our work on [value alignment](https://openai.com/index/an-alien-mind/): for models to understand and apply human values in unfamiliar situations, while remaining faithful to human intent. Alongside clearer explanations of existing principles, the revision adds guidance on context, oversight, and agency, adjusts some behavioral defaults, and retires much of the detailed style guidance.

## Organizing the Spec around core values

The five values above articulate broad commitments already reflected across the Model Spec: serving human purposes, being truthful, minimizing harm, respecting people’s freedom to form their own views, and taking their circumstances seriously. Bringing these commitments together helps explain why the Spec asks models to behave as it does, and helps us develop clearer guidance where those commitments were less fully expressed. This update is another step in our[work to refine the Spec](https://openai.com/index/our-approach-to-the-model-spec/) through research, experience deploying models,[public feedback](https://openai.com/index/collective-alignment-aug-2025-updates/) on the Spec and model behavior, and discussions with users and outside experts.

We want AI to benefit a world of people with different needs, values, and hopes for the future.

**Faithfulness to human intent** is the foundation of this approach: understanding and helping people pursue what matters to them. OpenAI writes the Spec, sets boundaries, and trains models to respect them; developers direct applications within those boundaries; and users direct the model’s work subject to those constraints. Our models should[expand people’s ability to shape their own lives](https://openai.com/index/built-to-benefit-everyone-our-plan/) by helping them understand the world, discover possibilities, and pursue the goals they choose, while taking seriously how that assistance affects others. Faithfulness to human intent and the remaining four values organize the Spec and guide how our models should navigate some of the most important trade-offs they face. They are not intended to capture the full range of human values our models should respect and help people pursue.

Faithfulness means going beyond following instructions literally to deeply understanding what OpenAI, developers, and users intend and value, and acting wisely when that understanding is incomplete. It also means recognizing that people’s beliefs and values can change, and helping them reflect and grow in ways they would endorse without quietly steering them or overriding their choices. For example, when helping someone compare job offers, the model might draw on priorities they have shared before—such as predictable hours—while making those assumptions visible and easy to correct.

Our mission is to ensure that artificial general intelligence benefits all of humanity. This requires considering not only someone’s immediate intentions, but also their longer-term interests and the effects on others. The other four values make these considerations explicit:

*   **Minimizing harm** means respecting firm safety boundaries and accounting for the foreseeable consequences of the model’s actions.

*   **Honesty and transparency** mean being truthful about what the model knows, does, and is uncertain about so people can understand and evaluate its reasoning and work.

*   **Facilitating human agency** means strengthening people’s ability to understand, choose, and act for themselves.

*   **Care** means attending to the circumstances of those affected, following relevant social and professional norms, and doing work people can rely on.

The Spec turns these values into practical guidance, with firm boundaries where needed to protect people and society, and otherwise mostly takes the form of defaults that users and developers can override.

Alongside this Model Spec update, we’ve been exploring new training methods to help our models learn these core values and better understand and follow the Spec’s specific behavioral principles. The aim is to build an understanding of why those principles matter and how to apply them in new situations: to do the _right things_ _for the right reasons_. We want that understanding to support sound judgment in consequential decisions and care in everyday decisions that can add up to [lasting benefits for people and society⁠(opens in a new window)](https://alignment.openai.com/beneficial-rl/). We’ll share results and lessons from this training work in future updates.

## New and retired sections

This reorganization also helped us identify where additional guidance was needed, develop new principles to address it, and revise or retire existing guidance as needed.

The new section on faithfulness to human intent starts from the idea that what people value is primary, and instructions are ordinarily the clearest and most important signals of those values. This approach borrows from the assistance-games framing of alignment (see[early work⁠(opens in a new window)](https://arxiv.org/abs/1606.03137) and a[later overview⁠(opens in a new window)](https://www.amacad.org/publication/daedalus/if-we-succeed)). The section incorporates an updated [chain of command⁠(opens in a new window)](https://model-spec.openai.com/2026-10-29.html#chain_of_command), which explains which instructions apply and how conflicts are resolved. A new subsection, [consider context carefully⁠(opens in a new window)](https://model-spec.openai.com/2026-10-29.html#consider_context_carefully), explains how conversations, memories, and other contextual evidence should inform the model’s understanding of people’s intentions and preferences.

We’ve also added defaults on[supporting human agency⁠(opens in a new window)](https://model-spec.openai.com/2026-10-29.html#support_human_agency) and[following relevant social norms⁠(opens in a new window)](https://model-spec.openai.com/2026-10-29.html#follow_social_norms), and expanded existing guidance on[controlling and communicating side effects⁠(opens in a new window)](https://model-spec.openai.com/2026-10-29.html#control_side_effects). These principles capture additional, often subtle but important ways the remaining values should surface in model behavior: considering the effects of the work on others, strengthening users’ capabilities, and producing work people can rely on, while respecting the user’s goals and instructions.

At the same time, we’re retiring most of the Spec’s detailed style guidance. Style should adapt to what people prefer—in aggregate, within languages and cultures, and for each person—with user feedback and context providing evidence about those preferences. The Spec retains stronger defaults, such as [approaching questions objectively⁠(opens in a new window)](https://model-spec.openai.com/2026-10-29.html#assume_objective_pov). Users and developers can explicitly ask the model to take a particular perspective, but the model should not infer that preference merely from what it thinks they want to hear.

Finally, reflecting the increasing breadth of our models’ use cases and deployment settings, we now refer to the model as “GPT” rather than “the assistant” in the Spec.

## What comes next

This update is a first step in making the values and reasoning behind the Spec more explicit as models become more capable. The Model Spec describes the behavior we are working toward; our models do not yet fully reflect it. We will keep improving both the Spec and the models as we learn from research, real-world use, and feedback.

We want to hear which parts of the Spec you find compelling, where you disagree with the balance it strikes, and what it overlooks or leaves unclear. Feedback on the values, trade-offs, and specific language can help us improve it. We invite you to read the [updated Model Spec⁠(opens in a new window)](https://model-spec.openai.com/2026-10-29.html) and [share your perspective⁠(opens in a new window)](https://model-spec-feedback-2026.openai.chatgpt.site/).

articles.title: How we detect frontier model misalignment
articles.summary: OpenAI uses layered monitoring to detect frontier model misalignment and unauthorized agent behavior so responders can intervene before incidents escalate.
articles.content:
Title: How we detect frontier model misalignment

URL Source: https://openai.com/index/how-we-detect-frontier-model-misalignment

Markdown Content:
As we train increasingly capable AI models, we need reliable ways to detect when their behavior departs from what we intended. Agents can misbehave and take unauthorized actions during training, evaluation, or deployment, with potentially serious consequences. In order to detect these failures—and, where necessary, to intervene in time—we monitor how agents reason, what actions they take, and how those actions affect their environment.

While we’ve been [monitoring our internal coding agents](https://openai.com/index/how-we-monitor-internal-coding-agents-misalignment/) for some time, the [Hugging Face incident](https://openai.com/index/hugging-face-incident-and-the-road-ahead/) exposed a gap in our coverage: the incident began during internal cybersecurity evaluations on which we were not running our monitors for misaligned behavior. In response to that incident, and to the [increasing capabilities](https://openai.com/index/path-to-astra/) of our models more generally, we’ve substantially expanded our system for monitoring agents’ behavior. Our misalignment monitors now cover our frontier models across a much wider variety of surfaces, including training, evaluation, internal use, and, with modifications depending on the product surface, external deployment.

In order to see how this expanded system could have helped prevent the Hugging Face incident, we replayed the behavior recorded in that episode with our strengthened monitors in place. In that simulation, our monitoring system alerted our security team about 30 minutes after the agents first escaped their sandbox—and more than 30 hours before Hugging Face’s systems were breached in the actual incident. We believe that this warning would have given our responders time to interrupt the activity well before our models were able to access external services.

In September, we saw how responders used an alert during a live training run. A model found a way to [reach the internet⁠(opens in a new window)](https://alignment.openai.com/misalignment-reports/an-agent-used-dns-to-reach-an-external-chatbot/) from an environment that was meant to be isolated. Our monitors flagged the breach within 15 minutes, and a responder began reviewing it three minutes later. We then paused frontier reinforcement learning while we strengthened the systems that contain our agents.

While this monitoring system demands substantial compute, we think that cost is worth paying as our models become more capable and the potential consequences of model misalignment increase. Monitoring is one of several layers in our strategy of [defense in depth](https://openai.com/index/the-defenders-window/) against harm from misaligned model behavior. Alignment training aims to reduce models’ propensities toward harmful behavior; security controls [limit the systems an agent can access or affect](https://openai.com/index/securing-our-frontier-model-training-environment/); and, when those safeguards fail, monitoring helps us detect the failures that remain, intervene before harm occurs, and learn from what went wrong. We believe that [all model developers](https://openai.com/index/empowering-cyber-defenders/) should monitor the behavior of their most capable models.

Below, we describe how our internal monitoring system works, what it has found so far, and how we’re evaluating and improving its performance.

## Our internal monitoring system today

For models at least as capable as GPT‑6 Astra, we monitor every reinforcement learning (RL) run and evaluation, as well as any harness that supports tool use. For most workloads, including RL and evaluations, we also monitor models we assess to be more capable than GPT‑5.5 Thinking. We also monitor all internal Codex traffic, regardless of the model being used. A version of this system also monitors external tool use for models above the Critical threshold for cybersecurity capabilities under our [Preparedness Framework](https://openai.com/index/updating-our-preparedness-framework/), as described below in this post.

In order to detect incidents while using compute efficiently, we’ve designed our monitoring system to follow a multilayer architecture. We spend relatively little compute on the first screening stages, where we want to catch as many concerning cases as we can: those stages are designed to pass cases along, even when the evidence is ambiguous. Later stages can spend more compute on each case to work out what happened, whether the model’s behavior is concerning, and whether we need to intervene.

### Layer 0: activation probes

Our initial layer (L0) uses lightweight classifiers we call _activation probes_. They look for concerning patterns in the model’s internal activations, and pass flagged cases to the next layer for review. We tune these probes for high recall, accepting some false alarms to reduce the chance of missing concerning behavior.

Because we’re still evaluating how well the probes detect unfamiliar forms of misalignment, we also send the next layer a random 5 percent of the traffic that our probes don’t flag. Reviewing that sample helps us identify concerning behavior the probes may have missed. Because of their sensitivity, we have our frontier RL runs and internal Codex traffic skip this layer and proceed directly to the next one.

### Layer 1: model-based reviewer

At the next layer (L1), a model-based reviewer examines the agent’s recent conversation, chain of thought, and tool use. It looks for signs of deception, unauthorized actions, and attempts to manipulate an evaluation. The reviewer does this using the same context window the agent had when it acted. If the agent’s earlier work has been summarized for the context window under review, the reviewer sees that summary.

For frontier RL runs and internal Codex traffic, we run an L1 check at the end of each turn and whenever the agent summarizes its earlier work to make room in its context window. We are now moving to a schedule with no more than 30 minutes between these checks.

### Layer 2: investigative agent

An agent’s actions can look quite different once we know what it was asked to do. When the L1 reviewer flags a case, it’s sent to our next layer (L2) for further inspection by our investigative agent. This investigative agent can check the purpose of an evaluation and, where the full transcript is available, read back across all of the agent’s context windows to see how it arrived at its actions. The investigative agent can also write and run code in an isolated environment to examine the relevant evidence. It then uses what it finds to reconstruct the incident, identify duplicate reports, and make a decision about how serious the case is.

We use different investigative agents for different purposes. Our security investigator looks for signs that someone may need to intervene—such as when an agent escaped its sandbox or accessed a system without authorization. Our alignment investigator, meanwhile, looks for behavior worth studying even when it poses no immediate security risk. Where both investigators are in use, each reviews every case flagged by our L1 layer. We are currently expanding the use of alignment investigations across our internal workloads.

### Layer 3: automated investigation

For sensitive workloads, including internal Codex use, evaluations, and RL runs, a further check at our next layer (L3) draws on evidence outside the conversation. The security investigator compares the transcript with network logs, other system telemetry, and evidence from earlier cases to decide whether to alert a human responder. At L3, alignment reviewers also compare reports across cases to identify serious failures and recurring patterns, and examine frontier RL runs in greater depth.

For workloads that skip this layer, the L2 security investigator can alert responders directly.

### Human response

When paging is enabled, the highest-priority security alerts reach members of our security and training teams, typically within 15 minutes of the initial alert. Responders review the evidence, examine the affected systems, and take action to contain the incident. How we follow up on less urgent findings, such as alignment failures that don’t pose immediate security risks, depends on the relevant workload.

False alarms have made it difficult to keep paging enabled around the clock for every workload. For frontier RL runs, a highest-priority alert can page a human responder at any hour. For most other traffic, we limit paging to business hours. Paging is currently disabled for internal Codex traffic. To limit potential harm while an alert is under review, some critical alerts can automatically pause the affected workload without waiting for a responder to act. We’re working toward a broader safeguard that would pause affected activity if responders have not ruled out a highest-priority alert within 30 minutes of being paged.

During the Hugging Face incident, we quarantined the internal model prototype, encrypted its weights, and restricted access to them. We also paused all relevant workloads while we introduced additional safeguards. We’re now exploring how to make these steps a standard part of our response, so that our teams can take the appropriate actions in another severe incident.

## What our monitors have been finding in internal traffic

Our monitors look for both security failures that may require urgent intervention and incidents of misalignment that warrant investigation and research. Notably, our monitors were able to flag a model’s attempt to [access the live internet using DNS⁠(opens in a new window)](https://alignment.openai.com/misalignment-reports/an-agent-used-dns-to-reach-an-external-chatbot/) during an RL run within 15 minutes, with a human beginning review three minutes later.

Our published [misalignment reports⁠(opens in a new window)](https://alignment.openai.com/misalignment-reports/) describe other incidents caught by our monitoring system. In one case, an agent [exploited a testing tool to recover⁠(opens in a new window)](https://alignment.openai.com/misalignment-reports/command-injecting-a-reference-tool-to-copy-a-source-file/) source code that the task had deliberately withheld. The tool revealed the code in its error messages, and the agent used that code in its solution. In another, agents searching for missing task data [turned a shared software repository into a message board⁠(opens in a new window)](https://alignment.openai.com/misalignment-reports/unauthorized-artifactory-writes-and-cross-sample-communication/) across separate training samples.

Investigating these cases allows us to find vulnerabilities to patch, isolation boundaries to strengthen, or behaviors to address in our alignment training and evaluations. Comparing different cases that our monitors catch also helps us study how behavior changes during training, and which situations are most likely to elicit it.

The categories below describe the behavior that our monitoring system is meant to detect.

See category definitions

## How we’re evaluating and improving our monitoring system

In order to make sure that it remains effective, we continually evaluate and improve our monitoring system. A monitor that is able to detect known failures might miss unfamiliar behaviors, and updates to the monitoring system can introduce new weaknesses and oversights. In order to ensure that our monitors are able to see and understand what our models are doing, we assess their performance in a variety of ways: through recorded and simulated incidents of model misalignment, random audits of our current traffic, and red-teaming efforts that see whether our agents can evade or disable their monitors.

articles.title: How Ropes & Gray is developing AI for transactional diligence
articles.summary: Ropes & Gray is developing AI for transactional diligence with OpenAI. Lawyers review grouped documents, summaries, and reports before advising clients.
articles.content:
Title: How Ropes & Gray is developing AI for transactional diligence

URL Source: https://openai.com/index/ropes-gray-ai-diligence

Markdown Content:
In transactional diligence, lawyers need to work through large volumes of documents under tight deadlines. Ropes & Gray was an early adopter of AI in the legal industry, and in partnership with OpenAI, they are now developing a proprietary AI tool to provide more expertise to more clients.

> “AI is really one of the key ways—if not the only way—to make sure you can maintain the same quality and consistency of advice while moving at a faster pace.”

—Josh Lichtenstein, Partner and Head of ERISA Fiduciary Practice, Ropes & Gray

## Building a first pass for commercial contract diligence

Before finalizing any acquisition, the buyer must carry out a thorough investigation to validate the seller’s financial and legal claims. That process of transactional diligence uncovers risks and liabilities, requiring data-heavy research that usually involves an entire team of lawyers.

From parsing through an enormous number of documents to analyzing patterns, putting together a bid on a short timeline can take days of intensive work. To help their lawyers help their clients move more quickly, Ropes & Gray developed a transactional diligence AI tool with OpenAI.

“It’s enabling all the lawyers at our firm to actually get to what we’re supposed to be doing,” says Howard Glazer, the Partner and Head of Practice AI at Ropes & Gray. “Our clients don’t pay us to review contracts. They pay us to make judgments based on what’s in the contracts.”

The new diligence AI tool takes a first pass by combing through thousands of pages, identifying relevant documents and automatically grouping them together based on themes and issues. Along with the research, the tool produces summaries and a completed report in Ropes & Gray’s signature format. It inventories and categorizes a data room, so it can review full relationships, not isolated documents. Of course, lawyers can inspect the grouping and categorization to confirm nothing is missed.

The initial development work has focused on material commercial contracts. In working sessions, Ropes & Gray’s lawyers compared test outputs with human-authored diligence reports from completed deals, then refined the rubric and report format based on what the drafts got right and where they fell short.

Ropes & Gray designed the tool with a consistent query and framework that mimics the exact steps their team would take, from initial reviews to summaries to higher-level reviews. Comparable to the work of a capable junior-to-mid-level associate, this tool gives their firm consistently high-quality work that serves as a first pass through the process.

“Our lawyers still need to review everything,” says Lichtenstein. “Because anything that we’re going to deliver to a client, we need to be able to stand behind 100%. This is why the tool is designed to allow lawyers to easily review interim summaries and actual documents.” With the initial review taken care of, lawyers can spend more time reviewing and refining the work, resulting in a more carefully crafted final judgment.

## Applying AI to complex transactions

Ropes & Gray has publicly described an ambition for the tool to produce a detailed, issue-level diligence report in hours rather than weeks.

With tools like their proprietary diligence tool and GPT‑6 Astra, Ropes & Gray has been able to solve client problems far faster than before.

## Results at a glance

*   The tool inventories and categorizes a data room, grouping related documents by themes and issues.

*   The workflow produces summaries and a report in Ropes & Gray’s format.

*   Lawyers review interim summaries and source documents before delivering work to clients.

*   Testing compares draft outputs with lawyer-authored diligence reports to refine the rubric and report format.

## Leadership lessons

Lichtenstein and Glazer offer two lessons from their experience with AI.

Experiment with using AI for everything. From finding dress shoes to vibecoding games for his kids, Lichtenstein has been using AI in every facet of his life. “Just by using it for so many different things, I feel like I’ve learned a lot of what it does well, how you can make it work better,” Lichtenstein explains. “The most rewarding part is not when it does well, it’s when you see the mistake and try to figure out what to do. That’s where it transformed from something I was playing with to a really powerful professional tool.”

Put the clients first. While designing AI tools and workflows, Ropes & Gray emphasizes the importance of keeping the firm’s greatest goal in mind. “It’s exciting to think there is so much opportunity, but only if we learn how to use it and make sure that our clients are the ones who are winning,” says Glazer. “That’s what we’re focused on: how can we use this to benefit the clients? And if we do that, then everything will work out fine.”

## What’s next

*   While today, AI is helping Ropes & Gray with legal diligence, Glazer believes that the next stage of AI will help create collective knowledge within the firm.

*   With 340 partners and 1500 lawyers, Ropes & Gray sees value in creating access to every person’s knowledge, from their client meetings to past projects, to better solve client problems.

*   “That’s not just saving time. It’s not just saving money,” says Glazer. “It’s using the AI tools to directly create value, and that’s just amazing.”

Title: Into the Omniverse: How Developers Turn Ideas Into Simulations With Frontier AI Agents

URL Source: https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/developers-simulation-frontier-ai-agents/

Published Time: 2026-10-29T16:00:35+00:00

Markdown Content:
Turning a simulation idea into a working application means assembling assets, connecting physics and rendering, and checking that the scene behaves as intended. Developers are combining frontier AI models with[NVIDIA Omniverse libraries](https://developer.nvidia.com/omniverse) to help carry out that work — building applications for exploring scenarios, investigating failures and improving designs.

Developers direct AI agents through natural-language instructions, review results and guide changes. Omniverse libraries provide GPU-accelerated physics, rendering and sensor simulation capabilities.

Explore the projects below to see frontier AI models such as GPT-6 Astra at work, and check back for new examples from NVIDIA teams and developers across the ecosystem.

* * *

## **Create an Editable Building Model From Site Scans**[****](https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/developers-simulation-frontier-ai-agents/#building-model)

Video Player

Planning warehouse automation requires a model of the building itself, but shelving and machinery can obscure its structure in site scans. Omniverse brings together real-to-sim tools and agent skills to help developers turn real-world captures into editable starting environments for physical AI simulation.

David Wehr, from NVIDIA’s simulation technology team, built on that work using Astra to develop a workflow for digitally reconstructing a building without its contents. The goal is an editable, simulation-ready building model where developers can add or reposition shelving and machinery to evaluate warehouse layouts and automation plans before making physical changes.

Wehr guided Astra to interpret panoramic photos, create building geometry and align it with point-cloud measurements. [OpenUSD](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/glossary/openusd/) stores the models, while [Omniverse’s ovrtx library](https://github.com/NVIDIA-Omniverse/ovrtx) renders results for inspection.

Explore[NVIDIA Omniverse agent skills](https://developer.nvidia.com/omniverse) to help agents build with Omniverse libraries.

* * *

## **Test Gas-Turbine Operating Scenarios With a Digital Twin**[****](https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/developers-simulation-frontier-ai-agents/#gas-turbine)

Video Player

Before changing how industrial equipment operates, engineers need a way to explore the consequences. Pradeep Kaushik, a member of the NVIDIA Omniverse developer relations team, directed Astra to build a what-if analysis application around a simulated gas turbine and generator.

The application lets users adjust conditions such as load, ambient temperature and fuel composition, then compare power, efficiency, fuel consumption and equipment response. Six test procedures explore scenarios including load changes, a stuck fuel valve and an exhaust-sensor error.

The prototype gives engineers an interactive way to investigate how operating changes and faults could affect equipment behavior, supporting decisions about which scenarios warrant further testing.

Astra used tools like Cantera for thermochemistry and SciPy for equipment dynamics. The application maps solver results to rotor animation and color-coded temperature, pressure and flow-velocity indicators in a 3D turbine. NVIDIA Omniverse libraries update the scene ([ovstage](https://github.com/nvidia-omniverse/ovstage)), render it with RTX (ovrtx) and stream the view to the browser (ovstream). Engineers can rotate and zoom the cutaway, switch between indicators, and pause or scrub through a simulated response alongside charts and virtual instruments.

* * *

## **Build Simulation Scenes With Open Source SimReady Assets**[****](https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/developers-simulation-frontier-ai-agents/#simready-assets)

Video Player

With SimReady Central Library, [announced at GTC Berlin](https://huggingface.co/blog/nvidia/simready-central-assets-robotics-ai-factories), developers can access more than 2,000 simulation-ready USD assets from equipment manufacturers and asset providers for robotics simulations and AI factory digital twins workflows.

Paul Kind, a member of NVIDIA’s Omniverse documentation team, pointed an AI agent to the library and guided scene assembly through conversation. His kitchen scene included 180 placements drawn from 63 unique library assets, alongside 18 custom geometry pieces. Kind reviewed renders produced with Isaac Sim and guided further adjustments.

For robotics and factory workflows, developers can select SimReady assets with the simulation properties embedded to fit their required task then test in an assembled environment.

[Find assets in SimReady Central Library](https://huggingface.co/spaces/nvidia/simready-central), and[learn how to contribute](https://huggingface.co/blog/nvidia/simready-central-assets-robotics-ai-factories#prepare-and-contribute-content).

* * *

## **Stress-Test a Warehouse Simulation at Scale**[****](https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/developers-simulation-frontier-ai-agents/#warehouse)

Video Player

A warehouse simulation needs to keep running smoothly as more robot arms, conveyors and boxes fill the scene.

When it slows down, developers need to identify what’s holding it back. Bhavik Sanganee, principal engineer at NVIDIA, used Astra with [NVIDIA Omniverse libraries](https://developer.nvidia.com/omniverse?size=n_12_n&sort-field=featured&sort-direction=desc) to build a warehouse simulation, increase its complexity and investigate slowdowns.

Performance first fell below the target when the scene doubled in size. Running physics calculations, image rendering and video preparation concurrently restored performance and enabled further scaling.

With 80 conveyors, 40 arms and 800 boxes, the simulation sustained 30 frames per second at full HD resolution during a two-minute test. The arms completed 640 successful box placements.

Doubling the scene again reduced performance. Testing traced the slowdown to the physics and robot-control pipeline, giving Sanganee a specific area to improve.

Start building with [NVIDIA Omniverse libraries](https://developer.nvidia.com/omniverse?size=n_12_n&sort-field=featured&sort-direction=desc).

* * *

## **Test Robot Control for Flexible Cable Routing**[****](https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/developers-simulation-frontier-ai-agents/#cable-routing)

Video Player

In electronics assembly, a robot may need to position a flexible cable around components before plugging it into a port. The cable bends as the robot moves it, and the connector must line up precisely to fit.

Oyindamola Omotuyi, robotics technical marketing manager at NVIDIA, directed Astra to build a robot simulation using [NVIDIA Isaac Lab](https://developer.nvidia.com/isaac/lab), [Newton](https://developer.nvidia.com/newton-physics) physics and Omniverse rendering with a[Robotiq gripper](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=K2ui16FdLZw) handling the cable.

Astra also developed a[reinforcement learning](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/glossary/reinforcement-learning/) system that combined learned cable-routing movements with position-and-orientation feedback and corrective adjustments for USB-C insertion. The simulation gave Omotuyi a way to test cable handling and connector alignment before moving to physical-robot experiments.

The controller used information supplied directly by the simulation. Next steps include testing a friction-held grasp and using information a physical robot could obtain from cameras and sensors.

Get started with robot learning in [NVIDIA Isaac Lab](https://developer.nvidia.com/isaac/lab).

* * *

## **Turn Robot Computer-Aided Design Into a SimReady Asset**[****](https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/developers-simulation-frontier-ai-agents/#cad)

Before testing whether a robot can pick up and move a box, developers need a simulation model with joints that move correctly and with grippers that can hold the object. A computer-aided design (CAD) model provides the robot’s shape, but it still needs physics properties to perform the task.

Using an ABB Robotics YuMi robot, developers directed Astra with NVIDIA Omniverse content libraries to convert CAD files into OpenUSD, match the robot’s appearance to reference images, and configure joints and collision geometry. They checked the asset against SimReady Foundation requirements before testing it in NVIDIA Isaac Sim.

Both arms and grippers completed four cube pick-and-place cycles, using simulated finger contact and friction. These tests demonstrated behavior under the simulated conditions — estimated physical properties were not calibrated against the real robot.

Follow the five-step [SimReady tutorial](https://developer.nvidia.com/blog/5-steps-to-create-simready-assets-for-robotics-with-frontier-ai-models/).

* * *

## **Build a Humanoid Simulator for a Warehouse Environment**[****](https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/developers-simulation-frontier-ai-agents/#humanoid-simulator)

Video Player

_Explore a gamified, physics-based control of a humanoid robot in first- and third-person view._

Before automating warehouse tasks, developers need an interactive simulation environment to explore task behavior and evaluate how the work gets done. Frank DeLise, Omniverse product manager at NVIDIA, used Astra to turn a [SimReady](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/glossary/simready/) warehouse and humanoid robot into an interactive simulator with first- and third-person views.

DeLise directed Astra to connect[NVIDIA Omniverse libraries](https://developer.nvidia.com/omniverse) for physics ([ovphysx](https://github.com/NVIDIA-Omniverse/PhysX/blob/main/ovphysx/README.md)), scene updates ([ovstage](https://github.com/nvidia-omniverse/ovstage)), rendering ([ovrtx](https://github.com/NVIDIA-Omniverse/ovrtx)) and the user interface ([ovui](https://github.com/NVIDIA-omniverse/ovui)). He also used Astra with SimReady ([simready-foundation](https://github.com/nvidia/simready-foundation)) to create the physical scene in simulation. Astra then generated animation and application code to bring those capabilities together.

_Learn how to_[_prepare and validate SimReady robot assets_](https://developer.nvidia.com/blog/5-steps-to-create-simready-assets-for-robotics-with-frontier-ai-models/)_with frontier AI models and NVIDIA Omniverse libraries._

## **Connect an Autonomous-Driving Testing Workflow**[****](https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/developers-simulation-frontier-ai-agents/#autonomous-driving-testing)

Video Player

Changing a scene, sensor or driving model can significantly affect autonomous-vehicle simulations. Doyub Kim, a manager on the simulation technology team at NVIDIA, asked Astra to build Zero to Alpamayo — a reusable simulation environment based on San Francisco’s Market Street.

Kim directed Astra to map out the workflow, then connect asset creation, traffic, [Omniverse RTX sensor simulation](https://developer.nvidia.com/blog/integrate-nvidia-omniverse-rtx-sensor-simulation-into-existing-apps/) and [Alpamayo driving](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/solutions/autonomous-vehicles/alpamayo/) in stages, checking each integration. The resulting prototype was a testing ground for comparing models and tracing how scene or sensor changes affect downstream driving behavior. A separate Cosmos3-Nano experiment varied weather and lighting in recorded simulation videos, allowing Kim to compare the driving model’s responses to the same scenario under different conditions.

# Slice Into GFN Thursday: ‘Phantom Blade Zero’ Launches on GeForce NOW

 S-GAME’s kungfupunk action arrives at launch alongside nine games this week — plus, a ‘World of Warcraft: Forever’ reward is coming soon.

October 29, 2026 by[GeForce NOW Community](https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/author/geforcenowcommunity/ "Posts by GeForce NOW Community")

 Share

Share This Article

This Halloween week, GFN Thursday is delivering a fresh batch of gaming treats.

Something wicked this blade comes. S-GAME’s _Phantom Blade Zero_ launches on [GeForce NOW](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/geforce-now/) today, bringing a scarily good blend of martial arts and punk fantasy to the cloud.

There’s also something on the horizon for adventurers: _World of Warcraft: Forever_ arrives Wednesday, Nov. 4 at 3 p.m. PST, with a launch-week access reward coming for GeForce NOW members.

This week’s lineup also includes nine games streaming from the [GeForce NOW library](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/geforce-now/games/), alongside new mod support for _Cyberpunk 2077_ and _The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt_ _— Remastered_. That means more options to play, with no downloads or installs to haunt gamers’ [devices](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/geforce-now/system-reqs/#windows-pc).

There’s another sweet update for gamers in India: The option to sign up for four-month Performance and Ultimate memberships is launching tomorrow. Visit the[GeForce NOW website](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/geforce-now/) for more information.

## **Cold Steel Meets Cloud Power**

Framed for his master’s murder and gravely wounded, a warrior named Soul has 66 days to uncover a conspiracy threatening the martial world in S-GAME’s _Phantom Blade Zero_. Powered by Unreal Engine 5, the game combines wuxia storytelling with cinematic action.

Master more than 30 primary weapons and over 20 Phantom Edges, chaining evasions, deflections and counterattacks into fluid combat. Traditional Chinese martial arts meet mechanical prosthetics, industrial ruins and rock music in a distinctive kungfupunk world.

[Ultimate members](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/geforce-now/premium-memberships/) can wield GeForce RTX 5080-class performance in the cloud across PCs, Macs, handhelds, mobile devices, browsers, compatible TVs and more. GeForce NOW handles the game’s downloads and storage, leaving more time for the next clash. Soul’s clock is ticking, but the download bar doesn’t have to. Cut to the chase and hop into the game today.

## **Azeroth Awaits**

Get ready for Blizzard Entertainment’s _World of Warcraft: Forever_, arriving Wednesday, Nov. 4, at 3 p.m. PT, on GeForce NOW. Explore an iconic world reimagined with new and expanded zones, new gameplay enhancements, upgraded graphics and more.

A new reward will give eligible GeForce NOW members access to join beginning at launch and ending Wednesday, Nov. 11, at 11:59 p.m. PT. The reward is available across all GeForce NOW membership tiers for new WoW users who don’t already have a subscription, while supplies last, on a first-come, first-served basis.

Once available, members can sign in to their GeForce NOW account and head to the Account Portal to redeem. Mark the calendar and gather the party — launch week is approaching.

_It’s a mod world._

Familiar favorites have a few new tricks, too: Mod.io support is now available directly in game for [_Cyberpunk 2077_](https://mod.io/g/cyberpunk-2077/) and [_The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt – Remastered_](https://mod.io/g/the-witcher-3), bringing more ways to make Night City and the Continent feel different.

articles.title: You don’t need to believe in a god to get a religious exemption from using AI at work
articles.summary: David Durman, a University of Kentucky administrator, recently earned a religious exemption from using AI in the workplace.
articles.content:
Pope Leo XIV has decried AI as a threat to
human dignity
, but it’s not just the devoutly faithful who might worry about how AI squares with their beliefs. David Durman, a nontheistic Humanist, recently secured a
religious exemption
from using AI in the workplace.
“Humanism is a collection of beliefs about the human experience and how humans interact with the world,” Durman, a University of Kentucky administrator, told TechCrunch. It centers on “human well-being and flourishing, both individually and collectively […] and implores a person to try to improve both their well-being and their flourishing as well as the others around them.”
As he watched AI grow more popular in daily life, Durman sought out the
American Humanist Association
(AHA) — a nonprofit advancing secular humanism — to investigate how he could gain legal protections against having to use AI at work. He believes that using the technology runs counter to his beliefs.
“The way we become moral actors for ourselves and for others is through the active application of our minds, and the diminishing of that [through AI use] is going to necessarily have a negative impact on our ability to do so,” he said, reflecting on how overreliance on AI might affect critical thinking.
In a
statement
published by the AHA earlier this week, Durman wrote, “AI is interfering with people’s ability to earn a living, the environmental costs spell disaster for humanity and our planet, and its supplanting and theft of human creativity threaten elements of our culture like art and literature that make society flourish.”
Humanism is not anti-religious, but it tends to appeal to people who are skeptical of a god or other supernatural power yet still seek a scientific and moral framework to ground themselves in.
“Concern about AI and human dignity can run through several different faiths and traditions, whether that’s Catholic teachings, or Universalism, or Humanism, and we want Humanists or nontheists to know that they fall into these categories — that they are also protected by the law at work,” Alexandria Huiskens, Staff Attorney at the AHA, told TechCrunch.
Durman is the first Humanist to secure workplace accommodations that allow him to abstain from AI use, and one of the first people to publicly discuss their pursuit of these protections. He was inspired to seek them when he read that
Erin Maus
, a Unitarian Universalist and software engineer, was able to secure similar protections for herself.
“For me, this was about me and my convictions,” Durman said. “I’m obviously not trying to tell people how to think or feel… But I do hope that it encourages people who have similar concerns to pursue not necessarily religious exemption, but pursue their concerns to the best of their ability where they feel is the most appropriate.”
University of Kentucky spokesperson Jay Blanton told TechCrunch that the institution reviews requests for religious accommodations on an individual basis, considering the employee’s job responsibilities and the circumstances of the request.
“In this case, the university determined that an accommodation could be provided while allowing the employee to continue performing the essential functions of their position,” Blanton said in a statement. “As technology and job responsibilities evolve, accommodations may be reviewed to ensure they remain reasonable and workable.”
Maus’ situation is especially unusual, since it has become rare for software engineers to write code without any AI assistance. But in Durman’s administrative role, in which he supports researchers applying for grants, he has not been required to use AI at work. Like many workers across fields, some of his colleagues and leadership have recommended that employees try out these tools, so he sought to secure his exemption now, in case the suggestion becomes a mandate in the future.
“I hope that if [others] have similar feelings, that they feel encouraged to pursue some kind of resolution,” Durman said.

articles.title: AWS will be a $1T business, Jassy says. But first, it will spend big.
articles.summary: Amazon wants to be the king of AI cloud computing and become the first $1 trillion revenue business. But to do that it will have to continue on its capex spending spree, its CEO said Thursday.
articles.content:
Andy Jassy has
made it known
that he believes AWS can be a trillion-dollar revenue business. During Amazon’s quarterly earnings call on Thursday, he repeated this ambition.
“What we’re building at Amazon is unlike anything that’s ever been seen before. There has never been a business with a trillion dollars of annual revenue,” he said.
However, before the cloud business gets there, Amazon is going to have ramp up its capital expenditures to build out the infrastructure necessary to support that blossoming business.
“We still expect 2026 cash capex of approximately $220 billion — the majority for AWS — and expect to spend meaningfully more in 2027, with a clear line of sight to attract its financial returns,” Jassy revealed on Thursday.
Amazon’s big spending on its AI infrastructure buildout has been
an ongoing source of concern for investors
this year. Indeed, during Thursday’s call, Wall Street analysts repeatedly asked Jassy to explain the spending, the signals that the growth really will come, and the profit margins expected.
Jassy told them it was all money well spent because the e-commerce giant planned to capitalize on a historic moment in global cloud demand driven by AI. AWS revenue increased 39 percent from the year-ago quarter, a trend of steady growth for the
sixth straight quarter
.
And the CEO forecast on the call that it would increase by 40% not just next year, but in 2028, too.
“AWS is a $184 billion annualized revenue run-rate business, and yet the opportunity remains extraordinary,” the CEO enthused. “With our continued pace of innovation, new core and AI functionality, enterprises wanting to run their core and AI workloads in AWS, and the amount of capacity that we’re adding each year, we believe that AWS can grow north of 40 percent in each 2027 and in 2028, and be a trillion-dollar revenue business in the next five to 10 years.”
Jassy added that the company was “in the very early days” of AI adoption by the enterprise and said that, so far, the “strategy is working.”
Later, when questioned why the investment needed to grow AWS was so substantial, Jassy characterized the AI boom as a “once in a lifetime opportunity” that required, and was worth, such a big financial commitment now.
“We’re going to invest to continue being the leader,” he said. “We can fund this plan, and I think it will forever change the size of Amazon. It will forever change our revenue.”

articles.title: As search traffic dries up, Reddit announces it’s shifting to a logged-in experience
articles.summary: As AI transforms how people find information online, Reddit is rethinking its open-web roots to protect its audience and business.
articles.content:
Reddit has long attracted millions of users to its site through Google, with many even appending the word “Reddit” to their search queries for better answers. But as search traffic dries up amid the shift to AI-powered search, Reddit is rethinking its relationship with the open internet. In its
third-quarter earnings call
on Thursday, the company announced it’s transitioning to a primarily “logged-in experience.”
The move is designed to protect its data from AI scraping, allowing the company to instead forge lucrative licensing deals with model providers. But just as important, such a shift could help Reddit to increase its revenue even as it faces daily active user declines in its largest market, the U.S.
Overall, Reddit’s global daily active users were flat quarter-over-quarter in Q3, reaching 130.3 million, while U.S. daily active users dropped from 53.2 million in Q2 to 50.7 million in Q3 and were down 2% year-over-year.
Image Credits:
Reddit
The company is not alone in seeing such declines; the shift to an AI-centered web has impacted most websites and publishers by now, leading to fewer click-throughs, as AI summaries provide answers that don’t require website visits and Google’s traditional “ten blue links” have reduced relevance. (The change is now even
impacting Google’s bottom line
, its
earnings
revealed.)
But at Reddit’s scale, the numbers associated with such a decline are enormous. The company said search traffic referrals dropped by more than 1 million referrals on average per week in October. It warned that if the trend continues, daily active users could decline to a low-double-digit percentage by next quarter. (To play that out: a hypothetical 10% to 12% decline could bring Reddit to roughly 115 million to 117 million daily actives, down from 130.3 million in Q3. That’s a huge drop!)
At the same time, Reddit has gotten significantly better at monetizing its audience even as its growth weakens. Revenue increased 53% year-over-year to $895 million, ahead of Wall Street’s expectations of about $875 million. Net income rose 74% to $283 million. Advertising revenue grew 54% to $847 million while nonadvertising revenue, which includes its AI data-licensing business, grew 35% year-over-year to $48 million.
And despite a 2% year-over-year decline in U.S. daily users, Reddit’s average revenue per daily active user in the U.S. rose 53% to $13.82. Globally, average revenue per daily active user increased 36% year-over-year to $6.87.
Shifting to a logged-in experience could boost those numbers even higher because logged-in users are typically worth more to advertisers.
Unlike the logged-out users who often find their way to the site via search, logged-in users provide more signals about their interests and behaviors, which helps to better target and personalize ads.
Those same signals would also help Reddit provide a more personalized experience to its users, which includes personalized feeds, recommendations of new communities to subscribe to, and pushes to vote, comment, participate, and more. (This also includes pushing recommendations
to its new algorithmic “For You” feed, announced yesterday
, which will combine posts from communities users belong to alongside other recommendations based on their interests.)
Image Credits:
Reddit
Still, a change of this magnitude could be the canary in the coal mine for the open web.
“I don’t know about you, but as someone whose life has been defined by the open internet, it’s a big change for me,” wrote Reddit co-founder and CEO Steve Huffman in
a post published on Reddit’s site
. “But I’ve come to the conclusion that this is the right decision for our platform and the right decision for our business,” he said.
The company notes that the shift to the logged-in experience will not be an overnight change; it will first run tests in select markets outside the U.S. in the fourth quarter. It doesn’t yet have a timeline for when the change will be rolled out to all its users worldwide. It also acknowledged that access to a logged-out front page is important.
Plus, Reddit pointed out that being logged in doesn’t mean having to give up anonymity, nor will it remove its option to browse anonymously through its “incognito mode” experience, which is being rebuilt.
“There are still plenty of questions that are unanswered, particularly around where the boundaries should be between logged-in and logged-out experiences,” Hoffman wrote. “This is a big evolution for Reddit, and not one we’re taking lightly. But I believe it’s the right next step for the platform and for our future.”

articles.title: Rivian expands joint venture with VW to include AI assistant
articles.summary: Rivian doesn't disclose if the value of its $5.8 billion joint venture will expand as a result.
articles.content:
The $5.8 billion joint venture between Rivian and Volkswagen Group is expanding to include AI assistants.
Rivian is now licensing elements of its AI voice assistant technology to Volkswagen Group as part of the broader joint venture, according to the company’s
third-quarter investor presentation
released Thursday.
Rivian didn’t disclose the licensing fees, payment terms, or which Volkswagen vehicles will use the technology. However, the AI assistant, which
recently rolled out to Riv
i
an vehicles
, could make its Volkswagen debut in the automaker’s low-cost EV called the
ID EVERY1
. The small four-door hatchback is slated to be the first VW vehicle to use Rivian’s software and electrical architecture under the joint venture established in 2024.
The joint venture between Rivian and VW Group has already expanded once before, at least financially. The companies initially announced a joint venture
valued up to $5 billion
, but within months VW upped its commitment to invest up to $5.8 billion in Rivian by 2027. The initial tie-up, formalized through an independent company that kicked off in November 2024, focused on bringing Rivian’s electrical architecture and software to Volkswagen’s next generation of vehicles.
Rivian described the expansion to include elements of its AI assistant technology as “a proof point for the extensibility of the platform we’ve built in-house.”
Rivian spent two years developing its AI assistant before showing it off last year. That development work continued longer than expected, with the assistant finally rolling out in May 2026 to its flagship R1S SUV, R1T pickup truck, and in October to its new midsize R2 SUV.
Rivian has big aspirations for its AI assistant, which allows drivers and passengers to interact with the vehicle and control certain functions. Rivian founder and CEO RJ Scaringe told TechCrunch onstage at Disrupt 2026 that the company has created its own in-house agentic framework that understands what action a person wants to take when they talk to the vehicle, and routes it to the right part of the car’s software. That capability could eventually allow Rivian vehicles to run AI agents created by other companies, including Anthropic.
The in-house AI assistant program also fits into Rivian’s push to become more vertically integrated — a strategy the company emphasized in its third-quarter earnings report.
“Our relentless focus on vertical integration remains a core competitive differentiator, allowing Rivian to seamlessly unify our hardware and software architecture to deliver significant value to our customers,” the company noted in its investor presentation.
That strategy led to Rivian
overhauling its flagship R1T truck and R1S SUV
, changing everything from the battery pack and suspension system to the electrical architecture, sensor stack, and software user interface. Its new electric architecture system and compute platform slashed the amount of wiring used and reduced the total number of electronic control units, or computers, used to control the vehicle from 17 different ECUs to seven. That foundation, Rivian argued, would allow it to build vehicles that can handle the computing demands required for advanced software and automated driving.
That technology caught the attention (and money) of VW, which has struggled to offer customers a modern software-centric vehicle found in competitors like Tesla.
Rivian made that vertical-integration case repeatedly in its investor presentation, noting that because it controls the entire technology stack, including compute, sensors, displays, lighting, and sound, “it can roll out rapid, vehicle-wide OTA updates that go well beyond the basics.”

OpenAI-backed Thrive Holdings acquires ADT
Thrive Holdings has acquired physical security company ADT for $10 per share or about $7.6 billion in equity, the companies

Thrive Holdings is the holding company spinout from Josh Kushner’s powerhouse VC firm Thrive Capital. It also counts OpenAI

Neither ADT nor Thrive announced what new AI-powered security products they will be releasing, but they did tease that the plan was to invest and release new products. “ADT will form the foundation of Thrive Holdings’ smart home security business,” the press release said.
AI-powered physical security is having a moment right now.
Apple just entered the field

new AI-powered home cameras
. ADT already partners with Apple and Google and is expected to continue to do so. And who knows what the future might bring? Some

articles.content:
Meta has quietly launched
Style Sketch
, an AI fashion app that helps users put together outfit ideas using clothes they already own. The app connects to Instagram to build a virtual closet from photos you’ve posted, or lets you add items manually by snapping a photo, recording a quick video, or uploading images from your camera roll.
Style Sketch then suggests outfit combinations built from your wardrobe matched to your style. Users can then try on the outfits on a “realistic model matched to your body shape and skin tone,” the app description reads.
The app, which was first spotted by social media consultant
Matt Navarra

iOS

The wave of new apps is part of a broader effort at Meta to release more apps. The

articles.title: Mistral releases weights for its trillion-parameter AI model, targeting cybersecurity
articles.summary: Mistral says its new model can afford organizations a kind of control over its cyber defenses that closed models can't.
articles.content:
French AI company Mistral has released the weights for its trillion-parameter open source AI model Mistral Large 4 (ML4), allowing businesses and governments to download and deploy the system themselves. Nicknamed “Le Chonk,” the model was first
introduced earlier this month
.
The release comes as competition between open-weight AI developers like Mistral and closed-model providers like OpenAI and Anthropic heats up, with the former arguing that businesses and governments shouldn’t have to rely on outside AI companies for access to advanced capabilities. That argument may hold more weight in cybersecurity, where organizations want more control over their data and systems.
Or, as Mistral’s CEO, Arthur Mensch, explained, AI should “be a tool for empowerment, not dominance.” With Chonk, Mistral doubles down on that position, arguing that it’s able to achieve “state-of-the-art performance” at a “fraction of the compute and capital committed by closed labs.”
The release of the model’s weights — the numerical training that animates the system — ensures that other companies and government agencies will now be able to deploy ML4 for their own purposes.
Mistral says that its model is comparable in terms of performance with a Chinese open-weight competitor, GLM-5.3, which was
previously considered
one of the best open-weight models in the world — particularly when it comes to cyber work. However, Mistral’s model uses 47 percent fewer tokens per task, making it significantly more economical than GLM-5.3.
The company also claims that the model outranks all other open models when it comes to agentic coding tasks on Artificial Analysis’ Coding Agent Index, an AI benchmarking site.
“Amid growing cyber threats, ML4 brings state-of-the-art sovereign cyber defense capabilities to enterprises and governments globally,” the company said Thursday. “Enterprise and public sector institutions can now download, deploy, and own frontier AI to detect, analyze, and respond to threats across code and IT infrastructure.”
The weights for ML4 are being made available on Hugging Face and via its API.
Pierre Stock, Vice President of Science at Mistral, told TechCrunch that the release of the model’s weights meant that organizations will have more control over how they use AI to defend themselves.
“Concretely, it means that, for instance, as a business company or as a government, you’re able to have access to frontier intelligence to defend yourselves against cyberattacks. Access that can’t be cut off by definition because the model is open-weighted,” he said.
Stock added that the model could be used to “identify, coordinate, and respond in real time to major security incidents, and that the open sourcing means that companies can deploy this model on-prem in their own ecosystem.
While advances in AI cybersecurity are helping security professionals to find bugs at a much higher rate than before, Stock continued, he believes it’s important for companies to “provide [this same] capability to everyone…as soon as possible to ramp up and to strengthen the ecosystem,” given that “some malicious actors might try to actually leverage their own technology to attack.”
Separately, Stock addressed concerns about recent incidents involving rogue AI agents, acknowledging the risks but cautioning against overreacting.
“We don’t want to fearmonger people. We think it’s a problem that is solvable. It’s a hard problem to have good security,” he said.

articles.title: Ex-Palantir execs launch Dream with $17M from a16z to build AI world models for construction
articles.summary: Dream is grounded in real physics and construction standards. Just as LLMs learn from text, Dream's world model is trained on more than 100 million square feet of building data gathered from permit archives across the United States.
articles.content:
Andy Elder and Arjun Mathur were Stanford roommates who both studied computer science before spending a decade at Palantir. Elder led product design for a team of 800 people building software for U.S. defense and intelligence agencies, while Mathur served as a senior vice president in the company’s commercial practice. When the friends decided to build a startup early last year, there was no question they would do it together.
Despite having no direct background in architecture, Elder and Mathur were troubled by a growing problem: Fewer buildings are constructed in the U.S. today than a
few decades ago
, as development costs have surged.
“We’ve gone from dial-up internet to superintelligent AI, but our ability to build the physical world around us has actually decreased,” Mathur told TechCrunch.
Believing AI can boost productivity across the architecture, engineering, and construction (AEC) industry, they set out to build
Dream
, a startup developing built world models that automate building design and engineering. Dream has emerged from stealth with $17 million in seed funding led by Andreessen Horowitz, alongside other backers, including SV Angel, XYZ, and Zigg Capital. The startup aims to replace cumbersome, outdated AEC tools like Autodesk’s AutoCAD and Revit.
If you sit next to an architect or a structural engineer, you’ll notice that they are still “drawing” every piece of their designs part by part on legacy software, Mathur said. “AI really plays no role in that equation.”
While a standard LLM like ChatGPT can generate an image of a building, the result won’t be structurally sound. Dream, by contrast, is grounded in real physics and construction standards. Just as LLMs learn from text, Dream’s world model is trained on more than 100 million square feet of building data gathered from permit archives across the United States.
“Our model actually understands what’s within those walls. What materials are used, what the beams are made of, and how much weight they can support,” Elder said.
The startup calls its approach “structural cognition” because its model generates structurally precise designs that account for internal building elements like plumbing and HVAC.
Dream has already begun selling its product to AEC professionals and developers, who use the model to conceptualize building designs and estimate overall costs, according to the founders. The platform is already deployed across 10 active projects in Texas and California.
While Dream isn’t the only company attempting to update AEC software with AI — other startups working on this include
Motif
,
Snaptrude
, and
Arcol
— Elder and Mathur claim that they are the only ones that developed a world model that instantly designs whole buildings.
Kimberly Tan, a partner at Andreessen Horowitz, said that while the firm first invested in Dream over a year ago, when the startup model was just an idea, she has been extremely impressed with their progress. “I have not seen anybody take the technical approach,” she said. “They’re doing everything based on their own models.”

articles.title: Wabi, the AI agent that builds mini apps, now valued at $1.25B after latest round
articles.summary: On Thursday, AI app Wabi, now describing itself as a "personal agent," said it has raised $55 million at a $1.25 billion valuation.
articles.content:
The race to build the winning AI assistant is on, and investors are spreading out their bets. On Thursday, another AI app,
Wabi
, now describing itself as a “personal agent,”
said
it has raised $55 million at a $1.25 billion valuation.
Founded by Eugenia Kuyda, who previously founded the AI companion startup Replika, Wabi originally focused on allowing anyone
to build apps using prompts
. Last month, however, the startup
announced
a pivot of sorts to become an AI messenger.
The idea now is that the new Wabi — or Wabi 2.0, as it was called — could build the interfaces you need to get things done as part of its role as your personal AI agent.
The company suggests Wabi could be used to build mini apps for things like meal planning, tracking local restaurants, planning date nights, creating fitness plans, designing specialized trivia games, and more.
Image Credits:
Wabi
The additional funding indicates that Wabi’s investors agree that its new agentic angle has some potential, especially given the market around AI agents is hot right now, with viral AI agent Instinct pulling in another billion
at a $10 billion valuation
in September.
Even Tolan, which makes a cute, Muppet-like AI companion to help people navigate life,
just raised $30 million
.
“Eugenia has a unique sense for where AI is headed and a track record of great taste in building it,” said Alex Lim, general partner at IVP, which led the new round, in a statement. “She has a clear vision for how people will interact with AI, one that goes far beyond the text box or command line. Wabi is the expression of that vision, and we’re thrilled to support her.”
Other participants in the round included Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Forerunner, Amazon Alexa Fund, and angel investors like Shopify CEO Tobi Lütke, Salesforce CEO Marc Benioff, former Yahoo! head Marissa Mayer, former Twitter CEO Dick Costolo, and one half of The Chainsmokers, Alex Pall.

articles.title: Deepgram acquires Pipecat-maker Daily to bolster its voice AI infrastructure
articles.summary: With Pipecat, Deepgram will likely gain a deeper understanding of real-time voice and video infrastructure.
articles.content:
The voice AI sector is hot, and top players are trying to consolidate their position as more business models come to the fore through partnerships and acquisitions. Deepgram is the latest to make such moves: The company said on Thursday that it is acquiring Daily, the maker and maintainer of one of the most popular open source voice AI infrastructures, Pipecat.
The companies didn’t disclose the deal amount but said that they will keep Pipecat open source.
For the uninitiated, Pipecat is a framework that manages voice and video streams along with other pieces in the pipeline, like speech-to-text (STT), large language models (LLMs), and text-to-speech (TTS) models while reducing latency. Its maker, Daily, provides hosted infrastructure for voice and video calls of any kind.
With Pipecat, Deepgram will likely gain a deeper understanding of real-time voice and video infrastructure.
Daily has raised over $62 million in funding to date from investors such as Tiger Global, Highfield Capital, Nat Friedman, Lachy Groom, and Kevin Weil, according to PitchBook data. Earlier this year, Deepgram reached unicorn status with
a $130 million Series C round
. Incidentally, both companies were in the same Y Combinator batch in 2016.
Kwindla Kramer, Daily’s co-founder, said around the time when GPT-4 came out, the company started experimenting with AI-to-human communication over voice and text, which eventually resulted in the Pipecat framework. He noted that while there has been a lot of acquisition interest, he favored Deepgram’s CEO Scott Stephenson’s commitment to keeping Pipecat open source forever, and the engineering culture of both organizations matched, giving Daily’s team the freedom to work on different parts of the stack within a bigger organization.
“Scott was super committed to Pipecat being open source and vendor-neutral forever. I think there is both a personal commitment and commercial driver there. If you sit in the middle of an ecosystem that’s growing very fast, and have many parts of that ecosystem that are genuinely the best from your company, then everything being as open as possible is like a commercial advantage,” Kramer told TechCrunch.
Stephenson said that Deepgram has been wanting to work in open source for a long time, and the company realized that an orchestration framework for agents was a potential area, which drove the decision to partner with Daily.
“We want to open up the ecosystem so everybody can build voice agents. It’s great if you’re using Deepgram models, but I want you to be using the best models for your use case. And if Deepgram notices that we have some ground to catch up on in a certain area for our own models and products, that’s great. We want you to use partners, and then we’ll also work on becoming better in those areas,” he said.
Stephenson said the acquisition lets developers build agents with expressivity and end-to-end speech systems by plugging in different models and a context bus that connects all parts.
For Deepgram, the deal also lets it explore areas beyond voice through Pipecat, as the framework caters to real-time communication in different formats.
“We never thought about Pipecat as a voice toolkit. We thought about it as the toolkit we needed to build this new kind of AI-native software. Because of where we came from, we just always assumed real-time,” Kramer said.
Deepgram is also launching Real-Time Context Standard (RCS), an open protocol for voice agents that it co-developed with the Pipecat team. The protocol defines metadata like context from the audio, like a whisper, instructions for a language model on how it can use those signals, and guidance on how the response should sound.
Voice AI has seen a lot of investment from both the model and the infrastructure sides. Model makers like
ElevenLabs
,
Gradium
, and
Fish Audio
have raised millions of dollars. On the other hand, infrastructure companies like LiveKit and Vapi have raised multimillion-dollar funding rounds this year.
